title: Risk, insurers and how insurance works
summary: Follow Tony's Pizza through its first year: the words of risk, five ways to handle it, insurable risks, reinsurance, and who owns and sells insurance.
objectives: Tell risk, exposure, hazard, peril and loss apart
Name the five methods of handling risk
List the traits of an insurable risk and explain the law of large numbers
Compare reinsurance, insurer types, ratings and distribution systems

scenes.title: Tony's Pizza: risk, insurers and how insurance works
scenes.subtitle: General Insurance: 10.5% of your exam, about 16 questions. The words of risk and how insurers work

beats.text: Opening night at Tony's Pizza in Detroit! A new brick oven, a full house, and more risk than Tony knows.
beats.say: Opening night at Tony's Pizza in Detroit! A new brick oven, a full house, and more risk than Tony knows.

scenes.title: Opening night: five words of risk
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: exposure, risk, hazard, peril; National Alliance glossary: loss; adapted from memory hook mn_core-01

draw.text: also a premium base, like payroll per $100

beats.text: Tony owns the shop, so he's subject to loss: his exposure. Exposure is also a premium base, like payroll per $100.
beats.say: Tony owns the shop, so he's subject to loss: his exposure. Exposure is also a premium base, like payroll per one hundred dollars.

beats.text: Will this oven ever start a fire?
beats.say: Will this oven ever start a fire?

beats.text: Nobody knows. That uncertainty is risk.
beats.say: Nobody knows. That uncertainty is risk.

beats.text: Greasy boxes pile up by the oven: a hazard, a condition that makes loss more likely.
beats.say: Greasy boxes pile up by the oven: a hazard, a condition that makes loss more likely.

beats.text: Friday, whoosh! The boxes catch fire. Fire, the cause of loss, is the peril.
beats.say: Friday, whoosh! The boxes catch fire. Fire, the cause of loss, is the peril.

beats.text: The burned value he claims is the loss: a reduction in value, the basis of a claim.
beats.say: The burned value he claims is the loss: a reduction in value, the basis of a claim.

scenes.title: Hazard, peril or loss?
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: hazard, peril; National Alliance glossary: loss; questions core-001, core-gen-05, core-gen-06; cp_personal-01 drill

items.text: Frayed, outdated wiring behind the oven
items.why: A condition that makes a fire more likely: a hazard.

items.text: The windstorm that tears off the roof
items.why: The windstorm causes the loss, so it is the peril.

items.text: The drop in value of fire-damaged flour
items.why: A reduction in value is the loss, the basis of a claim.

items.text: Poor housekeeping: trash piled in the kitchen
items.why: A condition that raises the chance of loss: the classic hazard.

items.text: The collision when a delivery van hits a parked car
items.why: Collision is a cause of loss: a peril.
The reduction in value is the loss.

beats.text: Your turn: hazard, peril or loss? The exam loves to swap hazard and peril.
beats.say: Your turn: hazard, peril or loss? The exam loves to swap hazard and peril.

reveal.text: The condition is the hazard. The cause is the peril. The drop in value is the loss.
reveal.say: The condition is the hazard. The cause is the peril. The drop in value is the loss.

scenes.title: Pure or speculative?
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: pure risk, speculative risk; National Alliance glossary: pure risk, speculative risk; question core-gen-03; hook mn_core-01
scenes.plain: Pure risk: loss or no loss, never a gain; generally insurable. Speculative risk can end in a gain or a loss.
scenes.example: A kitchen fire can only cost Tony. Opening the shop could make him money or lose it: that's speculative.
scenes.exam: Trap: a new business is speculative even though it could lose money, because a gain is possible. Speculative risk is generally not insurable.

beats.text: Pure risk: a chance of loss or no loss, with no chance of gain. It's generally insurable.
beats.say: Pure risk: a chance of loss or no loss, with no chance of gain. It's generally insurable.

beats.text: A kitchen fire can only cost Tony. Opening the shop could lose money, or make a lot.
beats.say: A kitchen fire can only cost Tony. Opening the shop could lose money, or make a lot.

beats.text: That's speculative risk, often called a business risk, and generally not insurable. Gambling is speculative too. Ask: could it end in a gain?
beats.say: That's speculative risk, often called a business risk, and generally not insurable. Gambling is speculative too. Ask: could it end in a gain?

scenes.title: Handle risk like a STARR
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: risk sharing, hold harmless agreement, avoidance, loss control, risk retention, self-insurance; hook mn_core-02

beats.text: Handle risk like a STARR: Share it, Transfer it, Avoid it, Reduce it, or Retain it.
beats.say: Handle risk like a STARR: Share it, Transfer it, Avoid it, Reduce it, or Retain it.

beats.text: Share: a group of pizzerias splits premiums and losses by a set formula, as reciprocals do.
beats.say: Share: a group of pizzerias splits premiums and losses by a set formula, as reciprocals do.

beats.text: Transfer: shift the financial hit. Buy insurance, or use a hold-harmless agreement: the other side takes on certain liabilities of yours.
beats.say: Transfer: shift the financial hit. Buy insurance, or use a hold-harmless agreement: the other side takes on certain liabilities of yours.

beats.text: Avoid: skip the activity. No deep fryer, no fryer fires.
beats.say: Avoid: skip the activity. No deep fryer, no fryer fires.

beats.text: Reduce: fewer losses, with driver training, or smaller ones, with sprinklers.
beats.say: Reduce: fewer losses, with driver training, or smaller ones, with sprinklers.

beats.text: Retain: pay losses yourself, through a deductible or self-insurance. A deductible retains the first part of each loss and transfers the rest.
beats.say: Retain: pay losses yourself, through a deductible or self-insurance. A deductible retains the first part of each loss and transfers the rest.

scenes.title: Tony's call: fewer delivery crashes
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: avoidance, loss control, risk retention; National Alliance glossary: transfer; questions core-002, core-gen-10

beats.text: Three fender benders this winter! How do I get fewer crashes and keep delivering?
beats.say: Three fender benders this winter! How do I get fewer crashes and keep delivering?

options.label: Stop delivering. No pizza runs, no crashes!
options.fail: That's avoidance: not doing the activity at all. It ends the delivery risk, but Tony wanted to keep delivering.

beats.text: The van sits parked while the phone rings and rings. Avoidance: no crashes, but no deliveries.
beats.say: The van sits parked while the phone rings and rings. Avoidance: no crashes, but no deliveries.

options.label: Send every driver to driver training
options.win: Driver training is reduction: it lowers how often losses happen, while Tony keeps delivering.

beats.text: Smart. Training cuts how often crashes happen, and the pizzas keep rolling. That's reduction.
beats.say: Smart. Training cuts how often crashes happen, and the pizzas keep rolling. That's reduction.

options.label: Pay for every crash himself
options.fail: That's retention: Tony keeps the losses and pays them himself. He wanted fewer crashes, and that takes reduction.

beats.text: Crunch! Tony pays each fender bender from the register. Retention: paying losses, not making them rarer.
beats.say: Crunch! Tony pays each fender bender from the register. Retention: paying losses, not making them rarer.

options.label: Buy insurance to pay for the crashes
options.fail: That's transfer: insurance shifts the financial hit to the insurer. It doesn't make crashes rarer, and Tony wanted fewer crashes.

beats.text: The insurer pays for covered dents, but the vans keep crunching. Transfer shifts the cost, not the crashes.
beats.say: The insurer pays for covered dents, but the vans keep crunching. Transfer shifts the cost, not the crashes.

reveal.text: Reduction makes losses rarer or smaller while you keep the activity. Avoidance drops it.
reveal.say: Reduction makes losses rarer or smaller while you keep the activity. Avoidance drops it.

scenes.title: What makes a risk insurable
scenes.src: Rejda & McNamara, Principles of Risk Management and Insurance (13th ed.); hook mn_core-03
scenes.hook: An ideally insurable risk is a CLEAN Deal: Calculable, Large numbers, Economically feasible premium, Accidental, Not catastrophic, Determinable.
items: Calculable chance of loss; a Large number of exposure units
Economically feasible premium; an Accidental, unintentional loss
Not catastrophic: a large share of units shouldn't be hit at once

beats.text: Tony's fire risk is a CLEAN Deal. Calculable: the insurer can estimate how often and how badly shops burn. Large numbers: thousands of pizzerias. Economically feasible: an affordable premium. Accidental: nobody plans it.
beats.say: Tony's fire risk is a CLEAN Deal. Calculable: the insurer can estimate how often and how badly shops burn. Large numbers: thousands of pizzerias. Economically feasible: an affordable premium. Accidental: nobody plans it.

beats.text: Not catastrophic: a large share of units shouldn't be hit at once. Watch out: EXCEPT questions may say the loss should be catastrophic. It shouldn't.
beats.say: Not catastrophic: a large share of units shouldn't be hit at once. Watch out: except questions may say the loss should be catastrophic. It shouldn't.

beats.text: Determinable: it's clear what caused the loss, when, where and how much. Textbooks word this list differently, so learn the six ideas.
beats.say: Determinable: it's clear what caused the loss, when, where and how much. Textbooks word this list differently, so learn the six ideas.

scenes.title: Ideally insurable, or not?
scenes.src: Rejda & McNamara (13th ed.); hook mn_core-03; IRMI glossary: pure risk, speculative risk; question core-gen-03

cards.text: An accidental fire at one of thousands of insured shops
cards.why: Only a loss is possible, it's accidental and measurable, and thousands of similar shops make losses more predictable: a CLEAN Deal.

cards.text: Tony's second shop might boom, or it might flop
cards.why: It could end in a gain, so it's speculative risk, which generally isn't insurable.

cards.text: Tony's cousin plans to burn down his own failing shop
cards.why: The loss must be accidental and unintentional. A planned fire isn't.

cards.text: A delivery van is stolen, one of many insured vans
cards.why: Only a loss is possible, Tony didn't plan it, it's measurable, and it's one of many similar vans: a CLEAN Deal.

cards.text: One storm hits a large share of insured shops at once
cards.why: Still a pure risk, but catastrophic: a large share of the exposure units shouldn't suffer losses at the same time.

cards.text: A loss no one can pin down: when, where, how much?
cards.why: The loss must be determinable and measurable: definite as to cause, time, place and amount.

beats.text: Swipe time: ideally insurable, or not?
beats.say: Swipe time: ideally insurable, or not?

reveal.text: A chance of gain, a planned loss, a catastrophe or an unmeasurable loss breaks the deal. Pure risk alone isn't enough.
reveal.say: A chance of gain, a planned loss, a catastrophe or an unmeasurable loss breaks the deal. Pure risk alone isn't enough.

scenes.title: The pool: how big, and who joins
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: law of large numbers; adverse selection; underwriting; questions core-005, core-bas-02

draw.text: More units: actual losses more likely to match expected
One fire can throw off the forecast
Losses likely land close to expected
A bigger pool makes the data more credible
My wiring sparks! Sign me up!

beats.text: The law of large numbers: the more independent exposure units, the more likely actual losses equal expected losses.
beats.say: The law of large numbers: the more independent exposure units, the more likely actual losses equal expected losses.

beats.text: Ten shops? One fire can throw off the forecast. Ten thousand? Losses likely land close to expected.
beats.say: Ten shops? One fire can throw off the forecast. Ten thousand? Losses likely land close to expected.

beats.text: Adverse selection is an imbalance: people who see a high chance of loss buy far more often than others.
beats.say: Adverse selection is an imbalance: people who see a high chance of loss buy far more often than others.

beats.text: My wiring sparks! Sign me up!
beats.say: My wiring sparks! Sign me up!

beats.text: Underwriting decides which risks to accept, how much insurance to write and at what rate. It exists largely to counter that imbalance. Large numbers is the pool's size; adverse selection is who joins.
beats.say: Underwriting decides which risks to accept, how much insurance to write and at what rate. It exists largely to counter that imbalance. Large numbers is the pool's size; adverse selection is who joins.

scenes.q: Tony's insurer grows from 1,000 insured pizzerias to 100,000. Under the law of large numbers, what happens?
choices: Each shop's own chance of a fire goes down
Actual losses become more likely to match expected losses
Premiums must rise to pay for catastrophes
scenes.why: A bigger pool makes results more predictable: closer to expected. It doesn't change any one shop's own chance of loss.

beats.text: Quick check: the pool grows a hundredfold. What happens? Pick an answer.
beats.say: Quick check: the pool grows a hundredfold. What happens? Pick an answer.

reveal.text: Actual losses become more likely to match expected. Watch out: no single shop's own chance of fire changes.
reveal.say: Actual losses become more likely to match expected. Watch out: no single shop's own chance of fire changes.

scenes.title: Who insures the insurer?
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: reinsurance, ceding company, treaty, facultative, capacity, surplus relief
scenes.plain: Insurance for insurance companies. For a premium, a reinsurer covers part or all of an insurer's liability.
scenes.example: Tony's insurer takes on thousands of shops, then passes part of that risk to a reinsurer. That makes the insurer the ceding company.
scenes.exam: Treaty: whole classes; the reinsurer must accept every risk that qualifies. Facultative: risk by risk; the reinsurer may decline.

beats.text: Who protects Tony's insurer? A reinsurer: for a premium, it covers part or all of the insurer's liability.
beats.say: Who protects Tony's insurer? A reinsurer: for a premium, it covers part or all of the insurer's liability.

beats.text: That makes the insurer the ceding company. Why buy? Capacity to write more, surplus relief, steadier results and catastrophe protection.
beats.say: That makes the insurer the ceding company. Why buy? Capacity to write more, surplus relief, steadier results and catastrophe protection.

beats.text: A treaty covers whole classes; the reinsurer must accept every qualifying risk. Facultative goes risk by risk; the reinsurer may decline.
beats.say: A treaty covers whole classes; the reinsurer must accept every qualifying risk. Facultative goes risk by risk; the reinsurer may decline.

scenes.title: The insurer's call: which reinsurance deal?
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: pro rata, quota share, excess of loss reinsurance; question core-008
scenes.ask: Which deal should the boss sign?

draw.text: We pay the first million. Help us above that!

beats.text: Quota share splits premium and losses at one percentage. Excess of loss pays only above the insurer's retention, up to a limit.
beats.say: Quota share splits premium and losses at one percentage. Excess of loss pays only above the insurer's retention, up to a limit.

beats.text: We pay the first million of any loss. Which deal helps us only above that?
beats.say: We pay the first million of any loss. Which deal helps us only above that?

options.label: Sign the quota share deal
options.fail: Quota share shares premium and every loss at the same percentage. Help only above a retention is excess of loss.

beats.text: The reinsurer takes its percentage of the premium on every policy in a class and pays that share of every loss.
beats.say: The reinsurer takes its percentage of the premium on every policy in a class and pays that share of every loss.

beats.text: Even the tiny claims?
beats.say: Even the tiny claims?

draw.text: Same split of premium and loss on every policy

options.label: Sign the excess of loss deal
options.win: Excess of loss pays the part of a loss above the ceding company's retention, up to a limit.

beats.text: A fire guts an insured office tower. The insurer pays the first million, its retention. The reinsurer pays the rest, up to a limit.
beats.say: A fire guts an insured office tower. The insurer pays the first million, its retention. The reinsurer pays the rest, up to a limit.

draw.title: Reinsurer: the rest, to a limit

reveal.text: Quota share, a pro rata form, splits by one percentage. Excess of loss starts above the retention.
reveal.say: Quota share, a pro rata form, splits by one percentage. Excess of loss starts above the retention.

scenes.title: Who's who in insurance
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: stock company, mutual company, reciprocal, Lloyd's; A.M. Best Guide (Version 121719); adapted from hook mn_core-04

spots.label: Stock company
spots.text: Owned by its stockholders, who paid in its capital fund. The stockholders need not be insureds.

spots.label: Mutual company
spots.text: Owned by its policyholders. Every owner is an insured, and every insured is an owner. Memory hook: "My policy makes me an owner."

spots.label: Reciprocal
spots.text: An interinsurance exchange: picture neighbors swapping risks. It's an unincorporated group of subscribers who pool risks, run by an attorney-in-fact.

spots.label: Lloyd's
spots.text: Not an insurance company at all. Lloyd's is an association and marketplace of independent underwriters.

spots.label: A.M. Best rating
spots.text: An independent opinion of an insurer's ability to meet its obligations. A++ and A+: Superior. A and A-: Excellent. Not a recommendation to buy.

beats.text: Tap each glowing spot.
beats.say: Tap each glowing spot.

reveal.text: Follow the owner. Stockholders own a stock company; they need not be insureds. Policyholders own a mutual.
reveal.say: Follow the owner. Stockholders own a stock company; they need not be insureds. Policyholders own a mutual.

reveal.text: My policy makes me an owner!
reveal.say: My policy makes me an owner!

reveal.text: A reciprocal: unincorporated subscribers pooling risks, run by an attorney-in-fact. Lloyd's is a marketplace of underwriters, not an insurer. A.M. Best: A plus plus and A plus, Superior; A and A minus, Excellent.
reveal.say: A reciprocal: unincorporated subscribers pooling risks, run by an attorney-in-fact. Lloyd's is a marketplace of underwriters, not an insurer. A M Best: A plus plus and A plus, Superior; A and A minus, Excellent.

scenes.title: Tony's call: who sells him the policy?
scenes.src: IRMI glossary: independent agency system, exclusive agency system, direct writer; question core-011

beats.text: Renewal time. A captive agent represents one company. A direct writer uses its own employees. An independent agent sells for one or more insurers.
beats.say: Renewal time. A captive agent represents one company. A direct writer uses its own employees. An independent agent sells for one or more insurers.

beats.text: I want someone who can shop around for me.
beats.say: I want someone who can shop around for me.

options.label: The captive agent
options.fail: A captive, or exclusive, agent represents only one company or a group under common management. Tony wanted someone to shop around.

beats.text: One company's policy, and that's it. A captive agent represents only one company or group.
beats.say: One company's policy, and that's it. A captive agent represents only one company or group.

options.label: The direct writer's salesperson
options.fail: A direct writer uses the insurer's own employed sales force, not independent agents. Tony wanted someone who sells for more than one insurer.

beats.text: He's on the insurer's own payroll: a direct writer's employee, not an independent agent.
beats.say: He's on the insurer's own payroll: a direct writer's employee, not an independent agent.

options.label: The independent agent
options.win: Independent agents sell for one or more insurers, and the agent owns the policy records and expiration data.

beats.text: I'll compare a few insurers for you.
beats.say: I'll compare a few insurers for you.

beats.text: She also owns his policy records and expirations: the data on when each policy expires.
beats.say: She also owns his policy records and expirations: the data on when each policy expires.

reveal.text: Exam tip: the independent agent, not the insurer, owns the expirations.
reveal.say: Exam tip: the independent agent, not the insurer, owns the expirations.

items: A hazard is the condition; a peril is the cause of loss
Pure risk is generally insurable; speculative can bring a gain
STARR handles risk; an ideally insurable risk is a CLEAN Deal
Quota share splits by one percentage; excess of loss, above retention
Stockholders own a stock company; policyholders own a mutual

beats.text: Ideally insurable risks are a CLEAN Deal.
